validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. A Russian Ministry of Energy public-servitude notice (mosertolovo.ru, a municipal government site hosting the federal notice) names this exact federal linear object ('...газопровода Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница... в составе стройки «КС «Северная» (газопровод Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница)') and lists dozens of cadastral parcels along its route through Vsevolozhsky then Vyborgsky District. A Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg subsidiary page (spb-tr.gazprom.ru, via Wayback) and an engineering contractor's project list (proektneftegaz.ru) independently corroborate the line's identity and ongoing maintenance/reconstruction activity through 2021. This is not a GEM-only or single-source entity.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified transmission gas pipeline (магистральный газопровод) -- confirmed by Gazprom's own subsidiary page language and energybase.ru's 'all Gazprom PJSC trunk pipelines' grouping.
DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate of P5590 (Leningrad-Vyborg-State Border II). The servitude PDF separately names 'Ленинград – Выборг – Госграница-2' as a distinct linear object in one parcel entry; proektneftegaz.ru separately lists reconstruction work scoped to '...Госграница-1' specifically (distinct from the joint '-1,2' references); spb-tr.gazprom.ru groups both under one branch's zone of responsibility as '-- 1, 2' (two named strings, not one). Identical LengthKnown/Diameter/Capacity on P2335 and P5590 is explained by both being genuine parallel строки (nitki) of the same corridor built to the same spec, not a copy-paste error -- consistent with how this batch's other twin-string pairs (Gryazovets-Vyborg I/II, Gryazovets-Leningrad I/II) are modeled.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner (Gazprom PJSC 100%) and Operator (Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg) both independently corroborated -- see fills[].
SPEC CAVEAT (the one open item): ru.wikipedia's 'Выборг — Иматра' history article states the original 1973-74 Leningrad-Karelian Isthmus-to-Finnish-border joint pipeline was built of 800mm pipe over a 160km route with 6 bcm/y capacity, opened with a Finnish-Soviet ceremony 9 Jan 1974 -- materially different from GEM's currently recorded 1220mm diameter, 115km length, and 9.13 bcm/y capacity. However, a genuinely independent, current, non-GEM technical database (energybase.ru) states exactly GEM's current figures (1220mm/115km/9.13 bcm/y), and documented ongoing reconstruction work (crane replacement, pressure-reduction-point reconstruction, КС Северная 2nd-stage compressor-station work) makes a diameter uprate and/or route realignment over 50+ years entirely plausible; the 160km history figure may also simply include the ~40-50km Finnish-territory stretch to Imatra/Valkeala that is out of scope for this Russia-only GEM row (which runs only to the state border). I could not find a document dating a specific reconstruction/uprate event, so I am NOT proposing a value change -- but flagging this so a future pass knows both figures exist in the record and why I left the current ones standing.

verifications.note: Database entry describes the line as an active Gazprom PJSC pipeline; lists 2025-10 and 2026-02 procurement/maintenance tenders scoped to this exact pipeline (e.g. 'Выполнение работ по устранению дефектов трубопровода на объекте Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница II' dated 2025-10-22, and technical-inspection tender dated 2026-02-24), which is itself dated evidence the line is still in active service.

Engineering contractor's project list names ongoing reconstruction work specifically on 'Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница-1' (control-unit/bypass reconstruction, manual-to-hydraulic crane replacement, pressure-reduction-point reconstruction at km 158) -- active maintenance/reconstruction investment confirms the line is in service, not abandoned.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: LastUpdated on the sheet is 2023-08-07; newest independent evidence found here is 2026-02 (energybase tender listing), well past that. The recorded Status=operating is still correct: this is the PIPE, not the export FLOW. Russia halted gas supply to Finland through the Imatra entry point on 21 May 2022 (independently confirmed via DW.com, 'Импорт газа через точку входа в Иматру прекращен' -- Gasgrid/Gasum statements) after Gasum refused to pay in rubles; Finland has sourced gas via Balticconnector from Estonia since. That is a change in EXPORT UTILIZATION, not evidence the physical pipe (Vsevolozhsky District to the state border) went out of service -- no source found states the pipe itself was shut down, mothballed, or decommissioned, and the dated 2025-2026 maintenance/reconstruction activity above shows continued investment consistent with the line remaining part of the operating Unified Gas Supply System (it can still move gas domestically within Leningrad Oblast / toward other consumers even with the cross-border flow to Finland halted). Per this batch's brief, this is the correct read: 'a line that has stopped exporting but remains in the Unified System is operating.' Recording this explicitly so a future pass does not re-litigate it. StartYear1=1973 also confirmed (see fills[]); no evidence found of a StartYear correction being owed.
